matches.quote: Methods are missing: how R□/layer is computed ... the contact geometry ... and how the MBE film thickness was determined.
The paragraph should be removed or replaced with magnetization data on comparable flakes, with background subtraction and sample mass or volume stated.
has no structural or compositional measurement on the flakes that were measured ... No Raman, TEM/SAED, micro-XRD, EDX or EELS is reported
The statement that "impurity-induced disorder in thin films cannot explain this phenomenon" (p. 6) is asserted, not tested.
no uncertainty on the boundary temperatures (220 K, 183 K, the dashed lines in Fig. 3), which appear chosen by eye ... inferred crossover temperatures
Samples 6 and 7 have the shorter c axis (11.592 Å), which the authors read as stronger distortion ... yet they are placed in the Bose glass region
Sample 4 (10 nm) and sample 5 (30 nm) superconduct ... address the non-monotonic thickness dependence directly or withdraw the claim that thickness is the control parameter.
The ρ ~ ln(1/T) versus σ ~ ln T discrimination is made by eye over windows too narrow to separate the two forms
L² = DT^−p with p = 1 is fixed without justification, and β scales as 1/p.
The comparisons with the 8/π factor of Fisher et al. and the ν = 5/2 Pfaffian state (p. 8), and the closing remarks on nickelates, are speculative
Define "Bose glass" as used. Conventionally it is an insulating, compressible phase with vanishing dc conductivity at T = 0
and the closing remarks on nickelates, are speculative and unconnected to the data; the Pfaffian has no evident connection to this system.
The superconductivity of samples 4 and 5, the endpoint of the whole SC–BG–FG picture, is assumed rather than documented in this manuscript.
Sample 4 (10 nm) and sample 5 (30 nm) superconduct, while samples 1–3 (25, 25 and 35 nm) are Mott-like ... ground state is therefore not set by thickness

notes: C15 is marked 'raised' because P6 and P7 directly point out that the claimed transition temperatures are visual departure points along smooth curves with no sharp feature and call them crossover temperatures. C4 and C3 are marked 'partly' because the review asks for missing device fabrication/characterization methods and primary superconducting data rather than the bulk synthesis recipe itself. C6 is 'partly' matched by P11, which challenges the empirical basis for attributing the resistivity reduction to octahedral distortion tuning correlations rather than disorder/impurities.
